jailor.summary: Default temporary cover: Veteran (TK). Disclose your Jailor identity when you need protection, must resolve a counterclaim, or can help Town act on a supported contradiction. Keep future prisoner choices and unneeded exact-role information private. This is a concealment preference, not a measured best strategy for every lobby.

options.why: Jail does not make an ordinary visit, so TK can conceal the power category without a nightly target story. Prisoners can still confirm a jail interaction.
options.bestWhen: Use the temporary cover while you can keep real jail history private without blocking protection or misleading a consequential Town vote.
options.exposure: A prisoner can identify a real Jailor interaction. Visitor reports or an alert claim can contradict your cover.
strategy: Answer TK during alignment claims; full-claim Veteran only if needed. Do not invent Alerts or visitor kills.
Keep your real prisoners, their claims and execution outcomes in a separate Jailor history.
Identify yourself as Jailor when protection, trusted coordination or a counterclaim makes it useful.
Drop the cover before Town relies on a Veteran ability or a false accusation caused by your story.

options.exposure: A missing shot, visit evidence, or pressure to demonstrate can end this cover.

mayor.summary: Default temporary cover: Veteran (TK). Reveal before a decisive vote when your extra influence can secure a supported execution, prevent a mistaken execution of you, or establish needed leadership. Do not wait until on trial. This is a concealment preference, not a measured best strategy for every lobby.

options.why: A quiet nonvisiting cover can conceal your growing vote power. It cannot supply an Alert, and your public Reveal ends the cover.
options.bestWhen: While unrevealed, when Town does not yet need your extra vote and no one is relying on a Veteran action.
options.exposure: You cannot produce an alert or visitor kill. Your Reveal publicly ends this cover.
strategy: Answer TK while hiding; use Veteran only as a temporary exact-role cover if pressed.
Do not invent Alerts, visitor kills or future bait that makes Town avoid protecting you.
Reveal before a decisive vote or before being put on trial, where Reveal becomes unavailable.
Once revealed, coordinate openly as Mayor; hiding is not worth losing a necessary vote swing.

options.why: A day-action cover avoids invented nightly investigations while concealing Marshal. Deputy shots and Tribunals are different public events.
options.bestWhen: Before Tribunal, while you can hold the cover without Town relying on a Deputy shot.
options.exposure: A Deputy shot and Tribunal are visibly different. You cannot meet a demand to shoot.
strategy: Answer TK during alignment claims; Deputy is a temporary cover if a full claim is needed.
Do not invent a shot or a miss. Hold your real Tribunal until supported cases justify it.

Use Prosecute when a supported case cannot safely be resolved by ordinary voting. This is a concealment preference, not a measured best strategy for every lobby.

options.why: Both public stories can wait for daytime evidence without nightly results. A Prosecution is a hanging, not a Deputy shot.
options.bestWhen: Before Prosecute, while concealing the power does not delay a necessary Town action or promise an unavailable shot.
options.exposure: A prosecution counts as a hanging; a Deputy shot does not. The public effects do not confirm the same role.
strategy: Answer TK initially; full-claim Deputy only as a temporary cover if pressed.
Build a supported case and check whether ordinary voting can already resolve it.
Do not invent a shot, a private miss or an attack result to make the cover look confirmed.
Disclose Prosecutor when useful and use Prosecute for a supported case; the public action ends this cover.

monarch.summary: Default temporary cover: Trapper (TP). Explain a consequential knighting, resolve a Monarch counterclaim, or share identity when it enables useful Town coordination. Separate proof of knighting from evidence of a Knight’s faction. This is a concealment preference, not a measured best strategy for every lobby.

options.why: A Trapper preparation night fits an N1 hold. Later placement stories must match actual Knight visits; neither matching travel nor knighthood supplies a real Trap.
options.bestWhen: After an N1 Knight hold, with later claimed placements matching your actual movement and no invented trap triggers or protection.
options.exposure: A Trapper must build before placing; your knighting nights and public Knights can contradict that schedule.
strategy: Answer TP while hiding Monarch; the default Trapper opening assumes you held Knight on N1.
If you Knight on N1 instead, change this cover first: a fresh Trapper cannot place a Trap on N1.
On later nights, match any claimed placement to your real destination; do not invent traps, triggers or saves.
Explain your real Knights and disclose Monarch when public vote weight, a counterclaim or Town coordination requires it.

options.why: On a night you actually Knight someone, a single-target protective story may share that destination. This is movement overlap only.
options.bestWhen: Only on nights when your actual Knight action shares the claimed destination, with no invented protection and no unresolved vote-weight explanation.
options.exposure: Knighthood is a public effect; a Cleric story cannot establish that you protected anyone. A held Knight action does not supply a visit.
strategy: Do not invent saves. Disclose Knight history when vote control or a contradiction makes it necessary.
